name: Keychain and Block Store persistence across reinstall
plain: A stored ID that survives uninstall, so a reinstalled app recognizes the person.
meaning: iOS Keychain entries remain after the app is deleted. Android needs Block Store or Auto Backup. Used for fraud and abuse limits, and sometimes tracking.

android.api_surface: Auto Backup (6.0), Block Store (Play services 2022), AccountManager
android.note: Cleared on uninstall otherwise; backups may restore app data on a new device.

ios.note: Items stay after uninstall; iCloud Keychain sync is optional. Not shared across different teams.

limits.headline: Can recognize you after a reinstall using an ID that stays behind on your phone
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app saves it quietly the first time you use it
can: Keep an ID in the iPhone Keychain that stays after you delete the app
Keep an ID in Android Block Store or Auto Backup that may come back
Sync the saved item to a new device if iCloud Keychain or Google backup is on
Tell the app you are a returning user
cannot: Share the ID with apps from other developers on iPhone
Survive on Android without backup or Block Store; a normal uninstall clears app data
Stay on a phone after a full wipe or reset
Come back on Android if you turn off backup
limits.differs: iPhone keeps Keychain items after uninstall by default. Android clears them unless backup or Block Store is used.

story.what_it_is: A stored ID that stays after you delete and reinstall the app.

marketing.name: Block Store
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: keep sign in data across app reinstalls and new devices, with no extra login steps.

story.for_you: You delete an app to start fresh, reinstall it, and it says Welcome back. You will not see the stored ID that told it who you were, and clearing it is not simple.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to stop abuse like repeat free trials, and to keep a person signed in after a reset. Ad and analytics firms also use it to keep a stable ID when the ad ID is blocked.

use_cases.example: A game recognizes a banned cheater who deleted the game and reinstalled, and blocks them again.
A streaming app limits a free trial to once per phone, even after you reinstall.
A store sees your welcome coupon was already used on this phone and does not give it again.
A bank app keeps your device trusted after an update, without a new text code.
A dating app spots someone returning after a ban and stops the new account.
An ad partner joins your pre and post reinstall activity, so attribution stays accurate.

story.android_note: Needs Block Store or Auto Backup. Data can also move to a new phone.
story.ios_note: Keychain items often remain after the app is deleted, unless the developer clears them.

technical_bounds: Apple: only same team; Android: Block Store is per app
Privacy label must declare any identifier collected

history.change: Block Store API released for credentials and IDs
